body:
## What to build

Preserve an integer Grouping set identifier when a SQLite expansion returns zero rows, including its supported direct materialization. A routine empty filter must not change the declared type of a package-created identifier.

## Reproduction and observed behavior

Confirmed on unmodified [6a5f611](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892), installed in an isolated library and exercised without testthat. R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dbplyr 2.6.0, DBI 1.3.0, RSQLite 3.53.3.

1. Open an in-memory SQLite connection and copy a one-row tibble with integer `x = 1L`.
2. Filter that lazy table to `x > 1L`, yielding no observations.
3. Call `expand_with_margins()` with `.id = "set"` and all other arguments at their defaults.
4. Collect the result and inspect the `set` column's R type.

Expected: zero rows and `set` equal to `integer()`.

Actual: zero rows and `set` equal to `logical()`.

The same empty local expansion and the populated SQLite expansion have integer identifiers. An empty SQLite summary with a requested identifier also returns integer after #653. Expansions with explicit rollup, all three sort modes, text/typed-missing labels, and compute followed by collect also reproduce the mismatch. DuckDB controls preserve integer.

An independent investigator used a nonempty, different two-row table filtered with `FALSE`, checked both label policies and all sort modes, and verified that the source stayed unchanged.

## Contract, diagnosis, and history

The [Grouping set identifier contract inherited by expansion](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/R/summarize_with_margins.R) explicitly promises an integer `.id` column even for a zero-row result. This is a package-created column; it is not a request to reconstruct the driver-dependent types of arbitrary ordinary aggregates.

The summary execution path registers an identifier's declared type for the SQLite result boundary, whereas `execute_margin_expand()` supplies no identifier declaration to `new_margin_execution()`. Consequently, empty driver inference leaks through the expansion path. The existing type fix must reach this caller as well, without inserting synthetic rows to force inference.

This is a follow-up to the boundary examined in #653 / #658. That issue's concrete reproduction and implementation covered Margin summaries; its empty-summary behavior is fixed and should remain so. The investigation confirmed this expansion failure at both `d4ea5f09d5698a6a89b68ecfd62ad450a4089bba` and `ad851dbefe99cf1cf6987dc5f0716f6a13d3873b` with the same dependencies. The defect predates #640; its first introduction is unknown.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An empty SQLite expansion with only `.id` supplied returns an empty integer identifier through direct collection.
- [ ] Cover filtered-empty input, explicit Grouping specifications, all sort choices, text and typed-missing labels, and supported compute followed by collect.
- [ ] Retain zero rows, column names/order, existing documented source-column type guarantees, and the existing integer identifiers for populated results.
- [ ] Keep #653's empty-summary share/identifier guarantees intact. Do not add synthetic partitions or promise types for arbitrary ordinary SQL expressions.
- [ ] Construction adds no unrequested input reads or new schema queries under ADR 0020. Add public-API regressions with local/driver controls and run the required package checks.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately). The finite-share collection defect concerns application of an existing declaration, whereas this ticket concerns the expansion identifier's missing declaration.
